subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 2-year-old girl of Southeast Asian ancestry is evaluated for chronic anemia. Hemoglobin is 8.4 g/dL, MCV is 61 fL, and iron studies are normal. Hemoglobin electrophoresis shows no abnormal hemoglobin, and genetic testing identifies a mutation in the polyadenylation signal (AAUAAA) of the alpha-globin gene.
question: Which of the following is the most likely consequence of this mutation?

options.text: Failure of 5-prime capping of the transcript
Absence of the poly-A tail, leading to rapid degradation of the mRNA before translation
Retention of introns because spliceosome assembly is prevented
Ribosomal stalling at a premature stop codon

explanation_correct: The polyadenylation signal AAUAAA directs cleavage of the transcript and addition of a poly-A tail by poly-A polymerase, an enzyme that requires no template. A mutation in this signal prevents tail addition, and the unprotected transcript is rapidly degraded before it can be translated, reducing alpha-globin output. This produces an alpha-thalassemia phenotype despite a normal coding sequence.

explanation_incorrect.A: Capping occurs at the 5-prime end and is independent of the 3-prime polyadenylation signal.
explanation_incorrect.C: Splicing depends on splice sites and snRNPs, not on the polyadenylation signal.
explanation_incorrect.D: Aminoacylation of tRNA is carried out by aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases and is unrelated to mRNA 3-prime processing.
explanation_incorrect.E: Premature stop codons cause termination and nonsense-mediated decay, but no premature stop codon is described in this patient.

educationalObjective: The AAUAAA polyadenylation signal is required for addition of the poly-A tail; its mutation leads to early mRNA degradation and reduced protein expression.
